title: ACOSH evaluates LN(x + SQRT(x*x - 1)), returning #NUM! when x*x overflows even where acosh(x) is finite
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ACOSH(x) evaluates LN(x + SQRT(x*x - 1)) via the worksheet LN kernel rather than a scaled asymptotic branch for large x. When x*x overflows binary64 (above sqrt(DBL_MAX)), Excel returns #NUM! even though acosh(x) is mathematically finite near 710: ACOSH(1.7976931348623157e+308) returns #NUM! while ACOSH(1.6449010616608172e+153) returns 353.48634664617043. Under cell Value2 delivery, ACOSH(1 + 2^-52) returns 2.1073424255447014e-08 (0x3e56a09e67ffffff), whereas literal formula entry can round 1+1e-16 down to 1 before evaluation. All 5,730 full-bank ACOSH rows match.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0 build 20430 (CalcFunc-Evidence runs/w111-extended-numeric-20260929/answers/answers-acosh.json.gz) and matched across 5,730/5,730 full-bank ACOSH rows.

correct.how: ln(2 * DBL_MAX) computed at 120 decimal digits in Python Decimal and rounded to nearest binary64.
